frequency_question: How often do executive principals follow through on sweeping unilateral tariff declarations within a short window when capability to execute via administrative authority is present?
membership_rule: Includes instances where a U.S. President declared specific tariff rates on specific trading partners with a set deadline; excludes general congressional legislative tariffs and purely rhetorical threats never advanced to executive order drafting.

cases.name: Trump Section 232 Steel and Aluminum Tariffs

provenance_note: claimed 9 hits but 8 of 10 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases
coverage_note: 10 named cases representing major post-WWII unilateral executive tariff deployments and high-stakes threats.
known_gaps: Minor retaliatory flickers involving very small trade volumes or sub-cabinet level anti-dumping duties are omitted as they do not match the principal-driven high political salience of this case.
skeleton: Presidential unilateral tariff implementation attempts divided into executed measures versus withdrawn/negotiated threats prior to effective date.
validity_reason: Base rate tied to the current executive administration's policy framework and institutional appetite for unilateral trade measures; expires with the presidential term.
